reason: Expects `toHaveJSProperty`, which compares a JavaScript property of the locator's element with Playwright's deep equality (Dates, nested paths, `undefined`). Strider has no such matcher, and no read of a property on a locator: `locator.evaluate` runs in the isolated world, which doesn't see properties the page's own script set

Expects `toContainClass`, which checks that an element's class list contains the given classes, each matched as a whole class. Strider's `toHaveClass` compares the whole class string or a regular expression and has no containment form

Expects `toHaveURL` with `ignoreCase: true`. Strider's `toHaveURL` takes no options, and a predicate over `page.url` would carry its own case-folding rule, which is the matcher's behavior, not the page's
Expects `toHaveAttribute` with `ignoreCase: true`. Strider's `toHaveAttribute` takes no options
Closes the page with a reason (`page.close({ reason })`), which the failed expectation's message quotes. Strider's `page.close` takes only `runBeforeUnload`

Passes an object to `toHaveURL` and expects Playwright's runtime error for it. Strider's `toHaveURL` takes a string or a RegExp by type, so the call doesn't compile. A JavaScript caller gets no such error: the object's `source` is undefined, which builds a RegExp that matches any URL
